chitchat: "Thin pan, thin cook. Buy iron once and be done."
She rings a skillet with a knuckle and listens to it the way other people listen to a doctor.
"Everything on that wall outlived the kitchen it came out of. Bear that in mind."
"You can have cheap, or you can have a pan. Not both, not from me."
description: A short, thick-forearmed woman with grey cropped to the scalp and two fingertips gone to the first knuckle on her left hand. She handles every piece that comes over the counter twice — once to weigh it, once to ring it — and prices it on the sound.

bye.text: She goes back to the rail, straightening handles that were already straight.

iron.text: "Heat's the whole job. Thin steel takes the flame and hands it straight to your food in one spot — that's how you get a black middle and a raw edge. Iron takes its time and gives it back even." She taps the skillet. "Costs more. Weighs more. Outlives you."

options.label: Why's the iron cost four times the steel?

root.text: "Look with your eyes first." She doesn't stop what she's doing. "If you want it down off the rail, say so."

shop.text: "Rail's the pans, casing's the small stuff. Range is there if you want to hear a pan before you pay for it."

clothing_layers: a scorched leather shop apron, stiff as board
a slate-grey work shirt with the sleeves cut off at the shoulder
a plain cotton bra and briefs

name: Tove Adaska
